newsitem.title: New Zealand: NZ shares close slightly easier in drifting market.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close slightly easier in drifting market.

text.p: * NZ market continues with lacklustre form
* Good turnover in Wilson & Horton
* Melbourne Cup day and U.S. election dull interest
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
123 nil * NZSE-40 cap index -3.04 at 2,311.46
322 -3 * NZSC cap index -13.02 at 4,786.88
372 nil * Volume $42 million. Futures -4, 1165
736 nil * Other movers - -10 +25
Melbourne Cup holiday fervour affected the New Zealand share market on Tuesday where it drifted in directionless trade to a near flat finish.
The top 40 index ended 3.04 points lower at 2,311.46 on modest volume of $42.4 million.
"The market here seems to be on holiday as well as Melbourne," said Cavill White Managing Director Don Turkington. "It's a market that has gone sideways.
There was little movement among the leaders -- Fletcher Paper gained four cents to $2.62 while Carter Holt Harvey fell three to $3.22.
Telecom was unchanged at $7.36 and Brierley Investments was steady at $1.23.
There was reasonable turnover in Wilson & Horton where its broker BZW picked up a line of 205,000 shares for bidder Independent Press Newspapers at $11.00/share.
New Zealand Refining gained $2.00 to $29.50 but on volume of just 1,050.
Elsewhere, there was interest in Independent Newspapers and Nuplex, where a line of 250,000 went through at $7.00, but few other features.
Brokers expect the market to continue to crab sideways this week. "It's really lacking momentum," Turkington said.
